body: Please provide a reproducible example with sample data: https://matthewrocklin.com/blog/work/2018/02/28/minimal-bug-reports

The above shows the inconsistency of the behaviour and should be reproducible (works in my Python console). For a true minimal example of the problematic part only, you can copy&paste the following:
```
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame(["a"])
print(df.replace({"a": 1.0, "b": 0.0}).dtypes[0])
```
This should print `float64`.
I suspect this is the same root cause as https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/issues/26632.
This bug is still present as of version 0.25.0. Bisecting with Kjilis minimal working example revealed the commit 720d263a9daa7a45e52a31d14ed9db1179c89cda to be the one which introduced this bug.

Thanks!

body:
This is indeed a bug .
```python
In [1]: import pandas as pd
   ...: df = pd.DataFrame(["a"])
   ...: print(df.replace({"a": 1.0, "b": 0.0}).dtypes[0])
object
In [2]: import pandas as pd
   ...: df = pd.DataFrame(["a"])
   ...: print(df.replace({"a": 1.0}).dtypes[0])
float64
```
When there is a scend replacer in the dict, the results are different. I've come up a solution to it in my PR
